instruction.text: Spell the word to find out what it means.

atoms.word: c o m p a s s

feedback.end: A compass is a tool that uses magnetism to help us navigate.

instruction.text: A compass works using magnetic metals. Select the part of the compass made of a magnetic metal.

feedback.finish: Correct! The needle of a compass is made of a magnetic material, and it works because the Earth has very strong magnetic poles. The point of the needle is attracted to the Earth’s North Pole, allowing us to always know what direction north is.

instruction.text: Select which direction magnetic north is for each person.

hint.text: Remember, the red pole of a magnet is north.

feedback.finish: Did you know that magnetic north is actually different from true north? Although, the two are still very close!

instruction.text: Use the image to fill in the gaps.

feedback.finish: This is true for any freely moving magnet! If you tie a bar magnet to a string and let it hang, it will keep turning until its north pole points to magnetic north!

atoms.b: The letters written on the compass represent the four cardinal directions: north, east, ((++south down)) and west.
The ((++needle person)) must be able to move freely in order to point north.
